newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Thousands of Indonesians yet to go home after riots.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Indonesians yet to go home after riots.

text.p: More than 3,000 Indonesians have not yet returned to their homes in west Kalimantan nearly a month after tribal rioting forced them to flee, a government official said on Friday.

"At least 3,000 people are still sheltered in Singkawang and Pontianak. They can't go home because their houses have yet to be rebuilt," the official told Reuters by telephone from the coastal city of Singkawang.
Pontianak is west Kalimantan's provincial capital on Borneo island.
The official denied a report from Republika newspaper which said the people had not returned to Sanggau Ledo district, 100 km (62 miles) away from Singkawang, because of safety reasons.
Thousands of people fled Sanggau Ledo early this month after the riot was sparked by a brawl between two groups of youths over a woman during a concert.

Five people died, nine were injured and dozens of houses were burned during the disturbances which erupted after a man from Madura island off the main island of Java reportedly stabbed two Dayak tribesmen in the stomach. The Dayaks are the natives of Kalimantan on Borneo island.
The official, who gave no other details, said some refugees had returned to their homes, particularly those whose houses were not badly damaged during the riot.

The rioters attacked people who came to Kalimantan as a part of the government's resettlement programme. Republika reported that local officials put the number of houses damaged during the riot at 976.

Last month, four people died after a mob went on a rampage in Tasikmalaya, setting fire to shops, buildings and churches. The violence was apparently sparked by reports of police brutality towards a Moslem religious teacher.
